As a community, the Church must practise love. Love thus needs to be organized if it is to be an ordered service to the community. As the Church grew, this radical form of material communion could not in fact be preserved. But its essential nucleus remained: within the community of believers there can never be room for a poverty that denies anyone what is needed for a dignified life.

31. The Church professes her faith in the Holy Spirit as "the Lord, the giver of life." She professes it in the Creed called Niceno-Constantinopolitan from the two Councils—of Nicaea (325) and Constantinople (381)—at which it was formulated or promulgated. There it is also added that the Holy Spirit "has spoken through the prophets."

These are the words that the Church receives from the very source of her faith, Jesus Christ. For according to the Gospel of John, the Holy Spirit is given to us with the new life, as Jesus foretells and promises on the great day of the feast of Tabernacles: "If anyone thirst, let him come to me and drink. He who believes in me, as the Scripture has said, 'Out of his heart shall flow rivers of living water.'" And the Evangelist explains: "This he said about the Spirit, which those who believed in him were to receive." It is the same comparison with water that Jesus uses in his conversation with the Samaritan woman, when he speaks of the "spring of water welling up to eternal life," and in his conversation with Nicodemus when he announces the need for a new birth "of water and the Holy Spirit" in order to "enter the Kingdom of God."

The Church, therefore, instructed by the words of Christ, drawing upon the experience of Pentecost and upon her own apostolic history, proclaims from the beginning her faith in the Holy Spirit as the giver of life, the one in whom the inscrutable Triune God communicates himself to human beings, making them sharers in the divine life. The Church also professes that the Holy Spirit "has spoken through the prophets": he spoke by the power of the Father and of the Son. And indeed it is by this power that he speaks in the prophets and in the Apostles, and in all those who, throughout history, bear witness to the Gospel.
